title: Living Without a Car
description: Four recordings about life without a car: a radio interview, a bus announcement, a family chat and a student talk.
instructions: Read the questions for each part first. Then press Play and listen. Choose the best answer for each question.

parts.title: Part 1 · A radio interview
parts.intro: You will hear Anna interviewing Mark, who sold his car two years ago.

script.speaker: Anna
script.text: Today on Green Living we're talking to Mark, who sold his car two years ago and hasn't missed it. Welcome, Mark.

script.speaker: Mark
script.text: Thanks for having me, Anna. Though I should say I did miss it for the first month.

script.speaker: Anna
script.text: What made you decide to sell it?

script.speaker: Mark
script.text: Money, mainly. When I added up the cost of petrol, insurance and repairs, it came to nearly three thousand pounds a year. And I only used the car at weekends, because I took the train to work.

script.speaker: Anna
script.text: So how do you get around now?

script.speaker: Mark
script.text: I cycle for short journeys, and I use the tram for everything else. For the odd occasions when I need a car, say, to move furniture, I rent one for a day. It's much cheaper than owning one.

script.speaker: Anna
script.text: Do you ever feel it's inconvenient?

script.speaker: Mark
script.text: Sometimes, when it rains and I'm carrying shopping. But honestly, I'm healthier now, and I've lost five kilos without even trying. I also talk to my neighbours more, because I walk past their houses every morning.

script.speaker: Anna
script.text: Would you recommend it to everyone?

script.speaker: Mark
script.text: Not to everyone. If you live in the countryside with no buses, it's almost impossible. But in a city, I think more people should try.

parts.title: Part 2 · A bus announcement
parts.intro: You will hear an announcement from a city bus service.

script.speaker: Mai
script.text: Good morning, passengers. This is an important announcement from City Bus Service about changes that start next Monday.

script.speaker: Mai
script.text: Route twelve, which goes from the station to the university, will now run every ten minutes instead of every twenty. It will also start earlier, at half past five in the morning.

script.speaker: Mai
script.text: Route thirty-five will be cancelled for three weeks, because of road work on Bridge Street. Passengers should take route nine and change at the market. Tickets will be valid on both buses.

script.speaker: Mai
script.text: We are also introducing a new weekly pass. It costs fifteen pounds and can be used on any bus or tram. Students can buy it for ten pounds if they show their student card.

script.speaker: Mai
script.text: Finally, please remember that the front doors are for getting on, and the middle doors for getting off. Thank you for travelling with us, and have a pleasant day.

parts.title: Part 3 · A family decision
parts.intro: You will hear Linh and her brother Nam talking about selling the family car.

script.speaker: Linh
script.text: Dad says he wants to sell the family car. What do you think, Nam?

script.speaker: Nam
script.text: Honestly, I'm a bit worried. How would we get to Grandma's house? There's no train, and the bus takes two hours.

script.speaker: Linh
script.text: Well, we could rent a car for that trip. Dad worked it out, and it's still cheaper than keeping ours.

script.speaker: Nam
script.text: Maybe. But what about the weekly shopping? Mum always does a big shop on Saturday.

script.speaker: Linh
script.text: There's a supermarket that delivers. Mum thought of it herself, actually. She said she'd be happy not to carry heavy bags.

script.speaker: Nam
script.text: Hmm. I suppose I could cycle to school instead of getting a lift. It would only take twenty minutes.

script.speaker: Linh
script.text: Exactly. And you'd get some exercise, which you badly need.

script.speaker: Nam
script.text: Very funny. Still, I'll miss sitting in the back seat with my music on the way to the beach.

script.speaker: Linh
script.text: We'll still go to the beach. We'll just take the train, and you can listen to music there.

script.speaker: Nam
script.text: Fine. I'm still not completely convinced, but I'll give it a try for a few months.

parts.title: Part 4 · A student talk
parts.intro: You will hear Minh giving a talk about a city for his geography project.

script.speaker: Minh
script.text: Hi, everyone. For my geography project I looked at cities that have fewer cars, and I'd like to tell you about one of them.

script.speaker: Minh
script.text: In this city, more than half of the people cycle to work or school. Forty years ago, the roads were full of traffic and the air was dirty, so the council decided to build safe bicycle lanes, separate from the cars.

script.speaker: Minh
script.text: At first, many shop owners were against the idea. They thought customers wouldn't come without parking spaces. But in fact, the opposite happened. People on bikes stop more often, so the shops sold more.

script.speaker: Minh
script.text: The city also made public transport cheap, and it built bridges just for bikes and pedestrians. Some of them are very beautiful, and tourists take photographs of them. In the evening, families often have picnics on them and watch the boats go by.

script.speaker: Minh
script.text: Of course, the plan wasn't perfect. Winters are cold, and some people still prefer cars. But the city shows that big changes are possible if people are patient. In my opinion, our town could learn a lot from it.
